design.approach:
M21 "Districts" — a metadata paint layer independent of OV.*, plus a Win95 "District Manager" dialog and SC2K low-zoom neighborhood labels. All three lenses agree districts are NOT an OV overlay (OV.* is one building per tile at sim.js:15; a district co-exists with whatever zone/road/plant occupies the tile), so they get their own per-tile channel.

DATA (sim.js City ctor, add beside the Uint8Arrays at ~line 293-305):
- `this.district = new Uint8Array(n)` — per-tile id, 0 = unassigned, 1..DIST_MAX. Indexed i=y*MAP+x like every array, so it inherits map-size handling automatically.
- `this.districts = []` — metadata `[{id, name, col}]`. RESOLVED conflict on color: `col` is an INDEX into a fixed module constant `DISTRICT_COLS` (12 Win95-friendly hex strings, near OV at top of sim.js), NOT a "#rgb" string (Depth) and NOT an HSL hue (Sim). An index keeps the save tiny, is deterministic, and makes every viewer/minimap/label paint identically with zero conversion. `name` is user text, default auto-suggested from the existing ST_NAMES pool for instant 1997 flavor ("Grunge Heights", "Dialup Flats"); cap length ~24.
- `this.distRev = 0` — ephemeral (like terrRev), bumped on every paint/erase/rename/recolor/delete; keys the render label-centroid cache. Not serialized.
- ID allocation RESOLVED: smallest-unused id in 1..DIST_MAX via a linear scan of `districts` (UIUX/Sim approach), NOT a monotonic nextDistId counter (Depth). Delete+create never leaks ids and nothing extra needs serializing.
- DIST_MAX = 12 (matches the 12-color palette; Uint8-safe). `newDistrict()` refuses past the cap via Snd.denied()/setStatus.

SIM METHODS (sim.js):
- `paintDistrict(x,y,id)` — if inMap and `district[i]!==id`, set it and `distRev++`. Paints on ANY land/water tile; never charges funds, never touches over[]. O(1).
- `newDistrict(name)`/`renameDistrict`/`recolorDistrict(id)` (cycles col index)/`deleteDistrict(id)` (zeros matching tiles in one O(n) pass, splices metadata, bumps distRev).
- `districtStats(id)` — pure read-only O(n) aggregator, called ONLY at dialog-open (see simIntegration for the cadence resolution): tiles, developed tiles, pop (Σ RES_POP[lvl] on ZR), jobs (COM_JOB/IND_JOB on ZC/ZI), avg landv/poll/crime, powered %, avg traffic on district roads, avg eduCov/medCov/polCov/fireCov, dominant zone.

TOOL (ui.js TOOLS:27-51): add `{ id:"district", name:"Distrct", key:"d", icon:"🏘️" }` (no COST entry → free, no tier lock). In applyToolAt (ui.js:486) add a branch BEFORE the `city.place` call at line 497: `if (UI.tool==="district"){ city.paintDistrict(x,y,UI.curDistrict); Snd.zone(); return; }`. It sits after the `lastPaint` dedupe (line 492-493) so drag-paint swaths dedupe for free, and returns before place()/toolOverlay()/COST so it can never write OV.NONE or mischarge. `UI.curDistrict` (new UI state, default 0=eraser) holds the active paint id. `setTool("district")` auto-opens the manager when no districts exist yet (discoverability). Name <input> in the dialog is safe against hotkeys because bindKeys already early-returns on `e.target.tagName==="INPUT"` (ui.js:515).

UI SURFACE — new `#dlg-districts` Win95 dialog (index.html, clone the `.dlg/.titlebar/.dlg-close` chrome of `#dlg-budget` at line 128), opened from a new Windows-menu item "Districts… 🏘️" and by selecting the tool. Classic listbox + stats-panel + button-column: a scrollable list, one row per district = color swatch + `▉ Name (n tiles)`, selected row = active brush, highlighted inverse-blue; a "(none / eraser)" pseudo-row at top sets curDistrict=0. Button column: New District (disabled at DIST_MAX), Rename, Color (cycles palette), Erase, Delete, Jump (centers camera on centroid), and "Paint" (selects the tool + closes). Right panel: a `<table>`/fieldset rebuilt from `districtStats()` on each open (same rebuild-on-open pattern as openBudget/openQuery) — pop, avg land value as a mini-bar, crime, pollution, jobs, dominant zone, powered %. Best/worst land-value rows get a highlight + a mayoral one-liner. All user text rendered via the existing `esc` helper.

MINIMAP: 7th mode. index.html #mapmodes (line 99) gets `<button class="btn95 tiny mm" data-mode="dist" title="Districts">Dist</button>`; the existing `.mm` click handler (ui.js:558) already sets UI.mapMode generically. Add a `mode==="dist"` branch in renderMinimap (render.js, before the default at ~line 1113): `col = city.district[i] ? DISTRICT_COLS[city.districts.find(d=>d.id===city.district[i]).col] : minimapDim(minimapCityCol(city,i),0.35)` (precompute an id→col lookup array outside the loop to keep it O(n)). Same dimmed-context treatment traffic mode uses (render.js:1104). Add an MM_LEGENDS.dist entry (ui.js:541) listing district swatches, and updateMapLegend already renders it.

MAP LABELS (render.js): new `drawDistrictLabels(city)` called at the end of renderFrame right after the drawCursor block (line 524-525), in SCREEN space (after worldTransform is restored) so text stays upright, not iso-skewed. A module cache `{rev, cents}` keyed on `city.distRev` recomputes per-district centroids (Σx,Σy,count → mean tile) in one O(n) pass ONLY when distRev changed. Each label projects its centroid via `(worldX(cx,cy)-cam.x)*cam.z + cvs.width/2` (render.js:79-80), drawn all-caps, letter-spaced, bold, dark stroke + translucent white fill, alpha ramping in as cam.z drops below ~0.7 (hidden when zoomed in so it never clutters detail work; full below ~0.45). Skip districts under ~6 tiles to avoid clutter. Additionally, when the district tool is active, drawCursor-style washes each districted tile in its color at ~0.12 alpha within the existing render cull window (render.js:320-323) for live paint feedback.
design.simIntegration:
RESOLVED the key cross-lens conflict: districts hook NONE of the simulation update path. recomputePower / recomputeAccess / recomputeTraffic / recomputeMaps / recomputeDemand / stampCoverage / growthPass / collectBudget are all UNCHANGED and never read district[]. tick() (24 ticks/month) is byte-identical whether or not any tiles are districted, protecting seed-determinism and per-tick cost. The Sim lens proposed folding recomputeDistricts() into recomputeMaps() every 14 ticks; I REJECT that — it adds an O(n) pass to the hot amortized path for data only ever viewed in a dialog, and it would make district stats "live" state that must stay consistent. Instead the Depth/UIUX cadence wins: stats are computed on-demand.

The ONLY coupling is one-directional and read-only, in `districtStats(id)`, which READS the outputs those systems already produce: over[]/lvl[] (→ RES_POP/COM_JOB/IND_JOB, the same tables growthPass uses, at sim.js:45-47), landv[]/poll[]/crime[] (recomputeMaps), traffic[] (recomputeTraffic), powered[] (recomputePower), eduCov/medCov/polCov/fireCov[] (stampCoverage). It aggregates them when the dialog opens — zero added work in tick(), no new dirty-flag plumbing. This IS the "integrate with the existing land-value map" requirement: the per-district land-value readout is the mean of city.landv[] over the district's tiles, sitting beside the existing "value" minimap mode.

Label centroids are the one thing computed off-dialog, but they read ONLY district[] (not any sim array) and are gated behind the distRev cache — recomputed only on a paint/edit, never per frame or per tick. So even the label path never perturbs sim arrays.

Mutation is isolated to the new methods (paintDistrict/new/delete/rename/recolor) invoked only from the tool and the manager; they touch only district[], districts[], distRev and never call any recompute*. Zone pop/jobs attribution is exact because zones are 1x1 (OV_SIZE at sim.js:31 lists only service/plant/stadium as 2x2, and those contribute no pop/jobs) — a 2x2 building straddling a district boundary affects only cosmetic tile/avg readouts, never pop/jobs accuracy.

bulldoze() and place() are left AS-IS: districts deliberately survive demolition/rezoning (SC2K behavior — a neighborhood boundary is administrative). Only the eraser swatch (curDistrict=0) or deleteDistrict clears tiles. Documented with a comment at the paintDistrict definition so it isn't "fixed" later.
design.saveImpact:
Bump serialize() `v: 8 → 9` (sim.js:1360). Add two fields alongside the existing Array.from serialization at sim.js:1376-1378: `district: Array.from(this.district)` (one MAP*MAP array, mostly zeros — same footprint and idiom as roadWear/plantYear/over/lvl, no RLE needed) and `districts: this.districts` (a tiny JSON list of {id,name,col} — JSON-safe as plain objects). Derived stats, centroids, and distRev are NOT serialized (same policy as landv/crime/traffic, which are recomputed/rebuilt on load) — keeps the save small and never stale.

deserialize() back-compat, mirroring the plantYear/roadWear precedent at sim.js:1400-1409:
- `if (Array.isArray(d.district)) c.district.set(d.district);` — else the ctor's zero-fill stands (a v≤8 save loads with no tiles assigned). TypedArray.set clamps naturally since size is restored first.
- `c.districts = Array.isArray(d.districts) ? d.districts.map(o => Object.assign({}, o)) : [];`
- `c.distRev` starts 0 (ephemeral); the first label draw builds the centroid cache fresh.
- NO change to the recompute chain at sim.js:1426-1427 — districts feed none of those systems, so nothing extra runs on load. Smallest-free-id allocation means no counter to restore.

Every existing save (v1–v8) round-trips unchanged (both fields absent → empty districts, all-zero layer, identical play). New v9 saves round-trip both arrays exactly; because districtStats is a pure function of the restored tile arrays, re-opening the dialog after save→load yields byte-identical stats — preserving the determinism-through-save invariant. Confirm no other code hard-checks `d.v === 8`; deserialize reads every field defensively, so an older build force-loading a v9 save simply ignores the district fields (graceful forward-compat).
design.risks:
- Tool-path regression (highest): a paint tool that isn't an OV must bypass place()/canPlace()/toolCost() or it writes OV.NONE and mischarges. Mitigation: the explicit `if(UI.tool==="district")` early-return in applyToolAt sits AFTER the lastPaint dedupe (ui.js:492-493) and BEFORE city.place (ui.js:497); keep "district" out of toolOverlay's map and out of COST. Verify with a paint→check-over[]-unchanged test.
- Cadence/coupling: none — districtStats is on-demand only, tick() and recomputeMaps are untouched, so no per-tick cost and no determinism risk. This is the deliberate rejection of the Sim lens's recomputeMaps hook.
- Save round-trip: both the layer and metadata are serialized as plain data; stats/centroids reproduce exactly from restored arrays. Verify a paint→save→load→re-stat cycle yields identical stats and identical label positions.
- Perf: districtStats O(n) gated to dialog-open; label centroids O(n) gated behind distRev (edit-only); label draw O(#districts≤12) per frame off the cache and only below cam.z~0.7; minimap "dist" is the same per-tile cost as the other six modes on the existing every-15-frame throttle (main.js:71). Precompute an id→col lookup outside the minimap loop to avoid an O(districts) find() per tile. The tool-active world tint is bounded to the existing cull window (render.js:320-323) and only when the district tool is selected.
- Label clutter/legibility on dense 128x128 maps: cap to districts ≥6 tiles, one uppercase line, dark stroke for contrast over any terrain, alpha only below cam.z~0.7, centroid-only placement.
- User-text safety: names render into HTML via the existing `esc` helper and into canvas fillText (inherently safe); cap length ~24. Name <input> won't fire tool hotkeys thanks to the existing bindKeys INPUT guard (ui.js:515) — regression only if that guard is removed.
- Palette/id exhaustion: DIST_MAX=12 matches the palette; disable "New District" at cap; deleting frees both an id (smallest-free scan) and a color. Far past realistic use.
- Orthogonality surprise: players may expect bulldoze to clear a district. Mitigate with the visible Erase swatch, a tooltip, and a documented comment at paintDistrict ("neighborhoods persist across rezoning").
- Discoverability of a costless metadata tool: three entry points — toolbar button, Windows-menu item, and the dedicated minimap mode with legend; setTool auto-opens the manager on first use.

criteria.statement: paintDistrict(x,y,id) assigns a per-tile district id into a dedicated Uint8Array channel (city.district), independent of OV.*: painting sets city.district[y*MAP+x]===id, and bumps the ephemeral city.distRev each time an assignment actually changes.

design.approach:
M22 = City Ordinances: citywide policy booleans toggled from a new Win95 dialog, wired as deterministic scalar modifiers into passes that ALREADY run. NO new OV overlay, no anchor, no tool, no minimap mode — all three lenses agree this is the honest call (ordinances are policy, not placed tiles; their effects are read spatially in the EXISTING crime/pollution/traffic minimaps). DATA MODEL (sim.js, declarative sibling of TOOLS/TIERS, ~line 105). One registry: const ORDINANCES = [ { id:"watch", name:"Neighborhood Watch", icon:"👁️", champion:"safety", minTier:1, blurb:"Block captains with walkie-talkies — cuts street crime.", cost:c=>Math.round(c.pop*0.03), mods:{crimeCut:14} }, { id:"recycle", name:"Citywide Recycling", icon:"♻️", champion:"environment", minTier:1, blurb:"Curbside blue bins curb industrial & roadway pollution.", cost:c=>Math.round(c.pop*0.045), mods:{pollMul:0.72} }, { id:"nostalgiaTax",name:"Arcade & Nostalgia Tax", icon:"🕹️", champion:"finance", minTier:1, blurb:"Sin-tax on arcades & Beanie Babies: revenue, but dents commercial demand.", revenue:c=>Math.round(c.comJobs*0.9), mods:{demC:-0.06} }, { id:"curfew", name:"Teen Curfew", icon:"🌙", champion:"safety", minTier:2, blurb:"Quiet streets after dark — safer, but the mall & arcade nightlife suffers.", cost:c=>Math.round(c.pop*0.03), mods:{crimeCut:18, demC:-0.06} }, { id:"carpool", name:"Carpool Incentive", icon:"🚗", champion:"transport", minTier:2, blurb:"Diamond lanes & rideshare boards ease road congestion citywide.", cost:c=>Math.round(c.pop*0.025), mods:{trafficMul:0.80} }, { id:"smoke", name:"Smoke-Detector Mandate", icon:"🚨", champion:"safety", minTier:2, blurb:"Fires are caught early — they burn out faster.", cost:c=>Math.round(c.resTiles*1.5), mods:{fireBurn:1} }, ]; const ORD = id => ORDINANCES.find(o=>o.id===id); - champion is the advisor key directly (safety/environment/transport/finance) — ordinances are not real departments, so no dept→advisor mapping layer. - minTier reuses the monotonic this.tier ratchet exactly like TOOL_TIER (Village=1, Town=2). - Registry is data-only; adding a 7th ordinance (e.g. Clean-Air Act T3, Tourism Blitz T3) is a one-row change, dialog/advisor/budget all pick it up. CITY STATE (constructor ~line 322, beside this.tier): this.ordinances = {} (id→true only when enacted; absent=off). Two derived caches, NEVER serialized: - this.ordMods = pop-INDEPENDENT effect scalars {pollMul, trafficMul, crimeCut, fireBurn, demR, demC, demI}, rebuilt by recomputeOrdinances() ONLY on toggle and on load. - ordNet is NOT cached (it scales with live pop/jobs) — computed fresh each rollover by ordinanceBudget() (see simIntegration). This resolves the depth-vs-sim conflict correctly: effect mods are static so cache once; § figures scale with counts so recompute at rollover. recomputeOrdinances(): starts from identity (pollMul=1, trafficMul=1, crimeCut=0, fireBurn=0, dem*=0), and for each o in ORDINANCES where this.ordinances[o.id] && this.tier>=o.minTier folds mods (muls multiplied, additives summed). The tier gate here means a hand-edited save that flips a locked flag applies NO effect until legitimately unlocked. Clamp defensively: pollMul/trafficMul floored at 0.5. enactOrdinance(id,on): validates unlock (this.tier>=ORD(id).minTier) else returns false; sets/deletes flag; calls recomputeOrdinances(). CURATED FEEL: two commerce-cutters (Curfew, Nostalgia Tax) both hit demC — you cannot stack every ordinance for free; that tension is the design, not a bug. Immediate legible feedback: toggle Recycling → pollution minimap recedes next recompute; enact Carpool → traffic map cools. Tier unlocks feel like rewards, announced in the Bugle. , OK/close; draggable free via bindDialogs titlebar handler. ui.js openOrdinances() generates one row per ORDINANCES entry (like the toolbar is generated from TOOLS): whole row is a
design.saveImpact:
Save format bumps v8 → v9. serialize() (line 1359-1360): change v:8 → v:9 and add ONE field: ordinances: this.ordinances (a small flat id→bool object, JSON-native, no Array.from). The ORDINANCES registry is code (never serialized); ordMods and the § figures are derived (never serialized).

deserialize() (beside the funding merge, ~line 1398): c.ordinances = (d.ordinances && typeof d.ordinances==="object") ? Object.assign({}, d.ordinances) : {}; Then call c.recomputeOrdinances() BEFORE the existing recomputePower/Access/Traffic/Maps/Demand cascade at line 1426 so ordMods is populated when those passes read it. Because c.tier is restored just after at line 1430, and recomputeOrdinances gates effects on this.tier>=minTier, order matters: set c.tier (move the tier restore, currently line 1430, to before recomputeOrdinances/the cascade) OR have recomputeOrdinances also run implicitly — simplest is to hoist the c.tier restore above the recompute cascade so the unlock gate sees the real tier. (tier is pure data, safe to restore early.)

BACK-COMPAT: a v8-or-earlier save has no ordinances field → {} → every ordinance off → ordMods all-identity (muls 1, additives 0), ordNet 0 → the city plays byte-identically to pre-M22. No typed-array resize, no per-tile state, no anchor change.

ROUND-TRIP: state is pure booleans with zero derived data saved; the recompute cascade already in deserialize re-derives every affected array from the restored flags, so save→load→save is exact. Unknown/removed ids in a tampered save are ignored because both recomputeOrdinances and ordinanceBudget iterate the ORDINANCES registry and read this.ordinances[id], not the reverse — forward/backward degrade gracefully. Missing keys default off. Locked-but-set flags (hand-edited save with tier<minTier) apply no effect and no cost (unlock gate) yet stay stored, activating cleanly once the tier ratchet reaches them — consistent with the sticky TOOL_TIER reward pattern.
design.risks:
DETERMINISM (lowest-risk axis): ordinances add ZERO new Math.random() draws — every effect is a static scalar multiply/add on an existing value or before an existing clamp, so the growthPass/fire RNG streams stay byte-aligned per seed and save round-trips exactly. The mods only shift the thresholds growth compares against; they consume no RNG.

PERFORMANCE: no new pass, no new per-tile loop. Each sim hook is one branch inside a loop that already runs (recomputeMaps/14 ticks, recomputeTraffic/5, recomputeDemand+growthPass/tick). recomputeOrdinances runs only on toggle/load over 6 rows. ordinanceBudget is O(1) over 6 entries using cached pop/comJobs/resTiles (resTiles folded into deptCosts' existing single pass — no new scan). Asymptotics unchanged, no O(map²).

REGRESSION: shared-loop edits all have an identity default when the flag is off (mul=1, add=0), so old saves and existing scenarios/tests behave identically until the mayor opts in — the same "100% funding reproduces legacy" invariant M23 relied on. Mitigation: precompute ordMods once; loops read cached scalars, never iterate the registry per tile. Verify by diffing a paused city's crime/poll/traffic overlays before vs after the patch with nothing enacted (must be identical).

BALANCE / STACKING: the two commerce-cutters (Curfew demC -0.06 + Nostalgia Tax demC -0.06) plus a tax hike could compound. Contained because all demand deltas pass through the existing clampD [-1,1]; keep each individual delta ≤0.06 and pollMul/trafficMul floored at 0.5 in recomputeOrdinances. This is a deliberate dilemma, tuned against a mature city before ship, not a defect.

ECONOMY EXPLOIT: Nostalgia Tax revenue scales with commercial jobs; kept modest (0.9/comJob) and self-limited by its -0.06 demC penalty (more tax → less commercial growth). pop=0/comJobs=0 → all costs/revenue round to 0, no treasury churn on an empty or all-residential map. Net routes through lastBudget.ord, visible and auditable in the budget table and City Hall records.

EDGE CASES: (a) tier only ever rises, so an unlocked ordinance stays available on a pop dip — intended, matches TOOL_TIER. (b) Effect gate on this.tier>=minTier means a hand-edited save flipping a locked flag applies nothing until legitimately unlocked, keeping the ratchet honest without needing to clear flags on load. (c) Toggling while paused must refresh overlays — handled by calling recomputeMaps/Traffic/Demand directly from the toggle handler, not waiting on tick. (d) deserialize must restore c.tier BEFORE recomputeOrdinances so the unlock gate reads the real tier (hoist the existing tier-restore line above the recompute cascade). (e) Advisor spam avoided by the enacted-off gate + metric threshold + existing ADV_REACT_TTL cadence; recs vanish once enacted.

criteria.statement: Enacting an ordinance rebuilds the pop-independent effect cache city.ordMods to the registry-declared scalars, and disabling reverts to identity. Specifically, on a city with tier>=1, city.enactOrdinance('recycle',true) returns true and sets city.ordMods.pollMul===0.72; city.enactOrdinance('watch',true) sets city.ordMods.crimeCut===14; toggling both off restores pollMul===1 and crimeCut===0.
criteria.check: Headless: construct/grab global city, force city.tier=2, call city.enactOrdinance('recycle',true) and city.enactOrdinance('watch',true); assert return true and city.ordMods.pollMul===0.72 && city.ordMods.crimeCut===14. Then enact both false; assert city.ordMods.pollMul===1 && city.ordMods.crimeCut===0. Confirm city.ordinances is a plain object with keys present only when on.

design.approach:
M24 = a second utility network that mirrors WIRE/power 1:1 so the risk surface stays tiny, framed as "power gates EXISTENCE; water gates DENSITY." One decision with a real tradeoff, plus a coverage-radius model (pipe in the street, buildings within reach tap in — the SC2000 model) so you don't pipe every lot.

OVERLAY-BASED PIPE (resolves the biggest cross-lens conflict). Adopt the Sim/UIUX choice: PIPE, WATERTOWER, PUMP live in the existing over[] array, NOT a parallel pipe[] array. Rationale: zero new serialized arrays (over[]/anc[]/lvl[]/varnt[] already round-trip), pipe is a strict analog of WIRE, no two-stage "I dozed it but water is still here" bulldoze UX, and the coverage-radius stamp (which all three lenses adopt anyway) makes Depth's "pipe under buildings" underground layer unnecessary. Cost: pipe cannot share a tile with a road (no PIPEROAD in M24 — explicitly out of scope, WIREROAD precedent noted for later) and we MUST add anti-crosstalk guards (see simIntegration). Net simpler.

NEW OV VALUES (append after WIREROAD=18, sim.js:27; never renumber — v9 pins these): PIPE=19, WATERTOWER=20, PUMP=21. OV_SIZE[OV.PUMP]=2 (tower is 1x1, pump 2x2 via the anc[] pattern like COAL). Predicates next to isPlant (sim.js:42): const isWaterOv=(t)=>t===OV.PIPE||t===OV.WATERTOWER||t===OV.PUMP; const isWaterSrc=(t)=>t===OV.WATERTOWER||t===OV.PUMP.

CONSTANTS (near POWER_CAP:67 / COST:85): WATER_CAP={[OV.WATERTOWER]:150,[OV.PUMP]:400} (served-tile capacity); WATER_REACH=3 (manhattan stamp radius); COST additions pipe:8, watertower:500, pump:2000; WATER_LABEL for the query panel.

THE TWO PROVIDERS (the decision):
- Water Tower (WATERTOWER, 1x1, §500, upkeep §15/mo): gravity-fed — needs NO power (works in a blackout), buildable ANYWHERE. The always-available, pricier-per-tile fallback so water is never un-buildable on a landlocked map. Caps 150 tiles.
- Water Pump (PUMP, 2x2, §2000, upkeep §40/mo): requires POWER (energized at anchor) AND at least one orthogonal TERR.WATER neighbour across its 2x2 footprint (hard canPlace gate — a dry pump can't be built at all, cleaner than a "dry pump serves 20" special case). Caps 400 tiles. Because the pump needs electricity, a blackout also dries that half of the city — the two utilities interlock. This is the fun tradeoff: cheap-per-tile ON a coast, unavailable inland.

DERIVED STATE on City (constructor ~sim.js:297, NONE serialized — all recomputed like powered[]/access[]): this.watered=new Uint8Array(n) (graded coverage/pressure map 0..255, 0=dry — literal stamp output); this.waterSupply=0, this.waterDemand=0 (ints), this.waterPressure=1 (float 0..1); this._waterReach=new Uint8Array(n) (BFS reached-tile scratch, allocated once, reused — no per-tick GC). Reuse the existing this.powerDirty flag as the shared utility-dirty flag (every place()/bulldoze()/waterfill()/fire-to-rubble already sets it); NO new dirty flag.

recomputeWater() — new method beside recomputePower (sim.js:~549), pure/deterministic, no Math.random:
1. watered.fill(0); _waterReach.fill(0); supply=0; seed queue q=[].
2. Seed energized sources: walk over[]; for each source anchor (anc[i]===i && isWaterSrc), energized = WATERTOWER always || (PUMP && this.powered[i]); if energized: supply += WATER_CAP[t]; mark every footprint tile in _waterReach=1 and push to q. (Pump power-gate mirrors stampCoverage's `if(!powered)continue`.)
3. BFS flood 4-connected from q, expanding into any neighbour j with over[j]===OV.PIPE (or a source footprint) not yet reached; set _waterReach[j]=1. Identical shape to recomputePower's flood, O(map).
4. Radius stamp (stampCoverage shape, max-combine): for every _waterReach tile, stamp watered[] over manhattan R=WATER_REACH with graded value min(255,(R-d)*40) — so zones near the network are served without a pipe on every lot.
5. waterDemand = count of consumer tiles (over∈{ZR,ZC,ZI}, lvl>=1, watered[i]>0); waterSupply=supply; waterPressure = supply>=waterDemand ? 1 : (waterDemand? supply/waterDemand : 1). If waterDemand>supply, pushMsg once "💧 LOW WATER PRESSURE — mains over capacity; build another tower or pump." NO per-tile RNG cut — pressure is a deterministic scalar consumed in growth.

UI SURFACE:
- TOOLS (ui.js:~37): contiguous utility trio right after the power plants — {id:'pipe',key:'p',spr:()=>SPR.pipe[5]}, {id:'watertower',key:'t',spr:()=>SPR.watertower}, {id:'pump',key:'u',spr:()=>SPR.pump}. Keys p/t/u are free. Cost chips render from COST automatically. toolOverlay() (sim.js:1454) maps the three ids.
- Sprites (sprites.js): SPR.pipe[16] blue-grey autotile via new pipeMask(city,i) (copy of wireMask, connects PIPE + isWaterSrc tiles) drawn FLAT at ground level like road (NOT overhead like wire); SPR.watertower a small silver/blue tank-on-legs (1x1); SPR.pump a 2x2 pumping station. Wire all three into spriteFor()'s switch (sprites.js:1627) — PIPE returns SPR.pipe[pipeMask(city,i)] and, because it is returned through the normal ground path (not the wire overhead special-case at render.js:407), it draws flat automatically. devRev++ already fires on build.
- Minimap: add <button data-mode="water" title="Water network">Wtr</button> after the Svc chip (index.html:99); ensure #mapmodes is flex-wrap so the 8th chip wraps at 800x600. New 'water' branch in renderMinimap (render.js:~1089): sources #0cf bright, watered tiles cyan scaled by waterPressure, dry pipe #234, else minimapDim(minimapCityCol,0.35) for district context (traffic-mode pattern). Extend minimapCityCol (render.js:1051): PIPE→'#2ad', WATERTOWER/PUMP→'#0cf'. MM_LEGENDS.water gradient bar (ui.js:541).
- Vitals/Query: index vitals gains <tr>Water<td id="v-water">0/0</tr> under Power; updateUI sets `${waterSupply}/${waterDemand}`. Query panel (ui.js:~921) gains <tr>Water<td>${city.watered[i]?'💧 yes':'no'}</tr> under Powered; the ovName list (ui.js:~905) extends with 'Water pipe','Water tower','Water pump'; a source anchor shows served/capacity + energized? like the plant rows. Pump's water-adjacency refusal surfaces through the existing red placement ghost (canPlace, render.js:1035) plus a setStatus hint ("pumps must sit next to water").
- Budget dialog: fillBudgetTable (ui.js:~710) adds a "Water system" row next to "Power plants".

PLACEMENT (canPlace/place/bulldoze, all over[]-based — no special arrays):
- canPlace pipe: 1x1, inMap, terr!==WATER (land-only; no water-bridging in M24), over===NONE (blocked on roads — no PIPEROAD).
- canPlace watertower: 1x1 land, over===NONE.
- canPlace pump: 2x2 footprint all land + over===NONE, AND ≥1 orthogonal TERR.WATER neighbour across the footprint; else return false (place() maps to setStatus "pumps must sit next to water").
- place(): pipe/tower go the normal single/marker path; pump uses the 2x2 anc[] loop like COAL (no plantYear — providers carry no age state). All set powerDirty=true (already in the shared path at :451).
- bulldoze(): unchanged — the 2x2 pump is removed via the existing anc[] footprint loop; powerDirty=true (:480). No two-stage bulldoze.
design.simIntegration:
ORDERING (the one cross-system coupling, one-directional power→water, no cycle): recomputeWater() MUST run AFTER recomputePower() because a PUMP reads this.powered[anchor].

tick() hook (sim.js:1304): inside the existing block, append recomputeWater after recomputeAccess:
  if (this.powerDirty || this.tickCount % 10 === 0) { this.recomputePower(); this.recomputeAccess(); this.recomputeWater(); }
Same cadence as power (every 10 ticks or on any over[] edit via powerDirty) — zero new scheduling, fully amortized, never per-frame. powerDirty is cleared inside recomputePower(); recomputeWater() reads powered[] before that matters since it runs in the same block.

CRITICAL ANTI-CROSSTALK (highest-risk item, from the UIUX lens — the three new overlays are all >= OV.ZR, so today's power code would treat pipes/towers/pumps as conductors AND consumers). recomputePower (sim.js:486) needs four exclusions:
1. conducts() (:492): add `&& !isWaterOv(this.over[i])` so PIPE/WATERTOWER/PUMP never carry electricity in the power flood.
2. demand scan (:518): add `&& !isWaterOv(t)` so water tiles are never counted as power consumers.
3. brownout scan (:532): add `&& !isWaterOv(t)`.
4. y2k scan (:543): add `&& !isWaterOv(t)`.
Sources are NOT energized by the power flood touching them; a PUMP is energized only via the explicit this.powered[anchor] check inside recomputeWater step 2 (the anchor tile still gets powered[] the normal way only if a WIRE feeds it — so a pump genuinely needs both a wire and a pipe). A WATERTOWER ignores power entirely. Add a smoke test: a lone pipe run must NOT power an adjacent zone.

growthPass (sim.js:889–935) — the only behavioural hook; water gates DENSITY exactly parallel to the existing eduCov/medCov level-2 cap at :924. Level 0→1 (:910–913) UNCHANGED (a shack has a well — needs only powered+road+demand), so a brand-new city plays identically until it wants density. In the upgrade branch (:914 `else if (dem>0.15 && lvl<3)`):
- Fold pressure into fit as a citywide growth damper (Depth): after the svc line (:922) add `fit *= 0.55 + 0.45 * this.waterPressure;` — a strained system slows upgrades without ever forcing anyone down.
- Extend the existing level-2 cap guard (:924) so it ALSO caps un-watered lots and pins level 3 behind pressure. Replace the branch condition with, effectively:
  if (this.lvl[i] >= 1 && !this.watered[i]) { /* no water → hard-capped at level 1 */ }
  else if (this.lvl[i] === 2 && this.eduCov[i] < 8 && this.medCov[i] < 8) { /* existing service cap at 2 */ }
  else if (this.lvl[i] === 2 && this.waterPressure < 0.9) { /* strained mains → no level-3 towers */ }
  else if (road && Math.random() < dem * fit * 0.42) { this.lvl[i]++; ... }
The gate is UPGRADE-ONLY — it never decrements lvl (the existing demand/gridlock downgrade paths at :929/:934 are untouched). This is the deliberate back-compat choice: no unwatered-decay counter (unlike power's unpow[]), so no pre-v9 skyline shrinks on load.

deptCosts (sim.js:1110): count pipes + tower anchors + pump anchors in the same over[] walk; return `water: Math.round(towers*15 + pumps*40 + pipeTiles*0.15)`. Flat upkeep, NO funding slider — mirrors the "plants: plants*40" line and leaves the M23 5-slider panel untouched (funding.water is a noted M23-style optional extension: one word in the funding default object + a slider that scales pump cap).

collectBudget (sim.js:1166): `const waterCost = dc.water;` add to net (`net = taxes - roadCost - serviceCost - plantCost - waterCost - debt`) and record `lastBudget.dept.water = dc.water` (+ a top-level `water: waterCost` field). fillBudgetTable reads it.

Fire/disaster: PIPE must be non-flammable — add `&& this.over[j]!==OV.PIPE` to the flammable predicates in fireTick (:967), ignite (:980), and the startDisaster fire-candidate scan (:997). Towers/pumps stay flammable like plants (2x2, demolished via the existing anc[] footprint loop, already set powerDirty). recomputeDemand, recomputeTraffic, recomputeMaps, recomputeAccess, nearestRoad, roadMask are all UNTOUCHED — water has no pollution/traffic/land-value/road-access effect in M24 (land-value tie-in noted as a future extension), and PIPE (like WIRE) is invisible to the road/traffic predicates.

deserialize (sim.js:1426): in the existing recompute block, add `c.recomputeWater();` immediately after `c.recomputePower(); c.recomputeAccess();` (before recomputeMaps is fine; it only needs powered[]) so watered[]/waterSupply/waterDemand/waterPressure rebuild from the loaded over[].

REGRESSION CHECKLIST (grep `OV.WIRE` for the exact analog sites): every over[]-indexed switch/array must learn indices 19–21 or new tiles render garbage / crash the query name lookup — spriteFor (sprites.js:1627), minimapCityCol (render.js:1051), the ovName list (ui.js:~905), deptCosts, and pipeMask. PIPE joins the wire-autotile connectivity path but draws flat (ground), not overhead.
design.saveImpact:
Version bump v8 → v9 (serialize sim.js:1360, `v: 9`). NO new serialized arrays — this is the central simplification won by putting PIPE/WATERTOWER/PUMP in the already-serialized over[] (with anc[] carrying the 2x2 pump). watered[], _waterReach[], waterSupply/waterDemand/waterPressure are all DERIVED and recomputed on load exactly like powered[]/access[]/polCov[]. Providers carry NO per-anchor persistent attribute (no aging à la plantYear), so no side table is needed. The save grows by zero fields; the v9 bump is essentially ceremonial — it pins the meaning of over[] indices 19–21 and hangs the new `c.recomputeWater()` deserialize step off the version.

Serialize change: exactly one edit — `v: 8` → `v: 9`. (funding is already serialized as an object, so if the optional funding.water slider is ever added it auto-carries; the deserialize `Object.assign({police:100,...})` default merge at sim.js:1398 just needs `water:100` added for old saves.)

Back-compat (forward-load of any v≤8 save), fully clean, no migration branch:
- A pre-M24 save's over[] contains no value 19–21, so pipe/tower/pump count is 0.
- The added `c.recomputeWater()` yields watered[] all-zero and waterPressure=1 (supply 0, demand 0 → the `demand?…:1` branch).
- Because the growth gate is UPGRADE-ONLY with NO water-decay counter, every existing zone KEEPS its current level — an old city with level-2/3 towers loads pixel-identical and plays identically. It only discovers that FURTHER densification (any lot trying to rise above level 1) now pauses until the player lays pipe from a tower/pump. This is the deliberate reason for "water gates upward growth" over "water mirrors power's unpow[] decay": a decay path would silently shrink every pre-v9 skyline on load — a save regression. Document this in the v9 deserialize comment exactly like the plantYear "no phantom decay on old cities" note and the M19/M23 default patterns.
- size inference (sim.js:1387) and all other fields untouched.

Older code loading a v9 save is rejected by the existing version check — the normal/expected direction. Round-trip is exact: recomputeWater is pure, and no water state is persisted, so save→load→recompute reproduces watered[]/pressure bit-for-bit from over[].
design.risks:
POWER/WATER CROSSTALK (highest, and the single must-not-miss item): the new overlays are all >= OV.ZR, so without the four isWaterOv() exclusions at recomputePower :492/:518/:532/:543 a pipe run would silently conduct electricity and inflate powerDemand/brownouts. Mitigation: add the four guards + gate source energization through the explicit this.powered[anchor] check rather than letting the power flood touch water tiles; add a one-line assert/smoke test (lone pipe does not power an adjacent zone; pump with pipe but no wire stays dry).

BACK-COMPAT DECAY: neutralized by design — the gate is upgrade-only and never decrements lvl, and pipe/tower/pump default to absent (over[] has no 19–21) on old saves, so no v≤8 city shrinks. If a future milestone wants water-starvation decay it must be scoped to "cities that have ever placed a provider" to avoid retro-punishing old saves — flagged, not implemented.

DETERMINISM: recomputeWater is pure (BFS flood + fixed-radius stamp + integer counting + one division), zero Math.random — stronger than the legacy power brownout, which DOES use Math.random for per-tile cuts. Pressure is applied as a deterministic scalar in growthPass (the `fit *= 0.55+0.45*pressure` damper and the pressure<0.9 level-3 gate), so the low-water effect adds no new non-determinism. Because watered[] is derived and never serialized, save round-trip is unaffected regardless. The only new RNG touch is the extra `&& watered[i]` condition in growthPass, which reads already-committed deterministic state — no read-before-compute hazard because recomputeWater runs before growthPass in the same tick and after recomputePower in deserialize.

PERFORMANCE: one O(map) BFS + one O(providers·R²)=O(providers·49) stamp + one O(map) count per power cadence (powerDirty or every 10 ticks), never per-frame — same order as recomputePower + one stampCoverage. At 128×128 (16k tiles) this is a few tens of thousands of ops, trivial. _waterReach is allocated once in the constructor and .fill(0) reused (like _trafficLoad), so no per-tick allocation/GC churn.

PLACEMENT UX: pumps refused unless orthogonally adjacent to TERR.WATER — risk players don't understand the refusal. Mitigation: the red placement ghost already renders from canPlace, plus a setStatus reason ("pumps must sit next to water"); the always-buildable tower is the landlocked fallback so water is never unavailable. Second UX risk: pipe cannot cross roads (no PIPEROAD), forcing routing around the grid — acceptable for M24, WIREROAD precedent shows the future fix.

RENDER GAPS: if spriteFor / minimapCityCol / the ovName query list / pipeMask aren't ALL extended for indices 19–21 in the same change, new tiles render as garbage or crash the query panel's name lookup, and PIPE would float like a power line if routed through the wire overhead path instead of the flat ground path. Mitigation: the grep-`OV.WIRE` checklist enumerates every site; PIPE explicitly returns through spriteFor's normal ground branch.

BALANCE: WATER_CAP (150/400), WATER_REACH (3), and upkeep (§15/§40/§0.15) are first-pass; the reach radius especially sets how dense a pipe grid must be. All are single named constants, none affect save format, so tuning is a one-line change with no migration.

criteria.statement: The core water mechanic exists and is measurable in the sim: OV.PIPE===19, OV.WATERTOWER===20, OV.PUMP===21 are defined (never renumbering 0..18), City exposes recomputeWater(), and after placing a WATERTOWER adjacent to a PIPE run reaching a developed zone tile, recomputeWater() produces watered[]>0 on served tiles, waterSupply>0 (== WATER_CAP for the tower, 150), and waterDemand counts the served consumer tiles.
criteria.check: page.evaluate: assert OV.PIPE===19&&OV.WATERTOWER===20&&OV.PUMP===21 and 0..18 unchanged; typeof city.recomputeWater==='function'. Build a tower+pipe next to a lvl>=1 ZR tile via city.place/canPlace, call city.recomputeWater(); assert city.watered instanceof Uint8Array, some watered[i]>0 within WATER_REACH of the pipe, city.waterSupply===150, city.waterDemand>=1, city.waterPressure between 0 and 1.

criteria.statement: The provider tradeoff integrates with power and terrain: a PUMP can only be placed with >=1 orthogonal TERR.WATER neighbour across its 2x2 footprint (canPlace returns false on dry land) and only contributes supply when its anchor is powered (this.powered[anchor]); a WATERTOWER contributes supply with no power. recomputeWater() runs AFTER recomputePower() so the pump reads fresh powered[].
criteria.check: page.evaluate: canPlace('pump') at an inland all-land 2x2 === false; at a coast tile (>=1 orthogonal TERR.WATER) === true. Place a coastal pump with NO wire feeding it, recompute: its footprint contributes 0 supply (waterSupply excludes it) / watered stays dry from it. Feed the anchor with WIRE so powered[anchor]===1, recompute: waterSupply increases by 400. Confirm tick()/deserialize call order invokes recomputePower before recomputeWater (grep source or instrument: temporarily flag powered read).

criteria.statement: Anti-crosstalk regression guard: PIPE/WATERTOWER/PUMP never conduct electricity nor count as power consumers. A lone PIPE run laid next to a developed zone must NOT power that zone, and placing pipes/towers/pumps must not inflate the power flood's demand/brownout counts versus an identical city without them.

Add a PIPE run touching an UNwired zone tile and recomputePower(); assert that zone tile powered[]===0 (pipe did not conduct). Add a tower and pump elsewhere, recomputePower(); assert the power-consumer/demand total is unchanged from baseline (isWaterOv tiles excluded at the conducts/demand/brownout/y2k scans).

criteria.statement: Water gates DENSITY, not existence: level 0->1 growth is unchanged (unwatered shack still upgrades to 1), but an un-watered lot is hard-capped at level 1, level-3 is pinned behind waterPressure>=0.9, and waterPressure damps upgrade odds — while the gate is UPGRADE-ONLY and never decrements lvl.

With full watered coverage and waterPressure===1, a lvl-2 lot can reach 3; with waterPressure<0.9 a lvl-2 lot is blocked from 3. criteria.check: page.evaluate: take a genuine v8 save object (or a v9 save with v forced to 8 and indices 19..21 absent), deserialize; assert no over[] entry in {19,20,21}, city.waterSupply===0, city.waterDemand===0, city.waterPressure===1, every watered[i]===0, and the lvl[] array equals the pre-load lvl[] (no decrement). design.approach:
M25 "Metro": rail + subway lines + stations on a SEPARATE PLANE, not in over[]. This is the load-bearing decision that resolves the three lenses. The Depth lens put RAIL/STATION/RAILROAD into the OV enum and needed a RAILROAD grade-crossing fused tile threaded through ~12 road predicates (nearestRoad, recomputeAccess, recomputeTraffic, trafficNear, roadWearTick, deptCosts, scanComplaints, roadMask, render/minimap). The Sim and UIUX lenses independently converged on a parallel Uint8Array plane. We take the plane: it eliminates that entire regression surface, gives subway-under-anything for free, shifts NO over[] byte values (clean back-compat, no collision with M26 WIREROAD=18), and reduces the sim edit to a handful of additive, guarded sites. From the Depth lens we keep all the RIGOR: the >=2-powered-stations network gate, the stampCoverage-verbatim catchment stamp, RAIL_MAX_SHARE=0.60, diversion-before-the-walk determinism, tick ordering, and the "Metro is open" milestone.

NEW STATE ON City (constructor ~278):
- this.rail = new Uint8Array(n) — the ONLY new serialized field. Enum next to OV: const RL = { NONE:0, TRACK:1, SUB:2, STATION:3 }. TRACK=surface (visible, can share a tile with a road = a grade crossing for free), SUB=subway (invisible except in the transit overlay + vents, runs under anything), STATION=1x1 rider magnet + network node + upkeep unit that bridges surface<->subway.
- Derived, NEVER serialized (rebuilt on load like access/traffic/coverage): this.railNet=new Int32Array(n) (component id, -1=none), this.stationLive=new Uint8Array(n) (1 iff a powered station on a >=2-station component), this.railCov=new Uint8Array(n) (0..255 ridership catchment, the "draws riders" map). Plus this.railRiders=0 (float, trips/mo diverted, for UI), this.railDirty=false (mirrors powerDirty), this.metroOpened=false (ephemeral, gates the one-time ticker).
- funding gains transit:100 (see saveImpact).

CONSTANTS: RAIL_STATION_R=7 (manhattan catchment), RAIL_MAX_SHARE=0.60 (a station diverts at most 60% of a zone's trips — arterials cool but never fully empty), station-power is by adjacency (below).

TOOLS (ui.js TOOLS array, after wind): {id:"rail",name:"Railway",key:"r",spr:()=>SPR.rail[5],minTier:TOOL_TIER.rail}, {id:"subway",name:"Subway",key:"u",spr:()=>SPR.subwayIcon,minTier:TOOL_TIER.subway}, {id:"station",name:"Station",key:"t",spr:()=>SPR.station,minTier:TOOL_TIER.station}. COST (sim.js ~85): rail:20, subway:45, station:300. Gate all three behind Town: TOOL_TIER.rail=TOOL_TIER.subway=TOOL_TIER.station=2 (the city "grows into" mass transit, matching the mayor/stadium reward-unlock pacing; place() already enforces TOOL_TIER>tier => {ok:false,reason:"locked"} at line 411, and the toolbar already dims locked tools via minTier). They drag-paint for free through the existing applyToolAt->place() path. toolOverlay() (sim.js 1454) is UNCHANGED — rail tools intentionally return OV.NONE there (so sizeOf=1) and are dispatched by tool id inside place(), because they write rail[] not over[].

SPRITES (sprites.js buildSprites): SPR.rail[16] autotile set built exactly like SPR.road/SPR.wire (loop m=0..15 over EDGE arms) but drawing two parallel steel rails + sleeper-tie hatching, baked ~8px raised so surface track reads over the street; SPR.subwayIcon (toolbar) + SPR.subwayVent (a small grate drawn only in transit overlay); SPR.station a brick depot with platform canopy and a "T" placard, built through the existing withNight()/spr.night path so an active station gets lit windows. New railMask(city,i) mirrors roadMask() but reads the rail plane: a cell connects to a 4-neighbor when that neighbor is TRACK||SUB||STATION (so surface, subway and stations autotile into one continuous line).

MINIMAP: 8th button in index.html mapmodes strip: <button class="btn95 tiny mm" data-mode="transit" title="Rail & subway network">Rail</button>. render.js renderMinimap gains a mode==='transit' branch mirroring 'traffic': surface TRACK steel-blue #6cf, SUB dim dashed #55f, STATION white dot (cyan #2ff if stationLive), zones tinted by railCov so the catchment reads, everything else minimapDim(minimapCityCol(city,i),0.35) for district context. Add MM_LEGENDS.transit (ui.js ~541). This is where the invisible subway becomes visible — the authentic Win95 data-layer toggle. minimapCityCol stays unchanged (rail is off over[]); the transit branch reads city.rail directly.

ON-MAP RENDER (render.js tile loop): after the existing over[] overlay block, add a rail-plane block reading city.rail[i]: TRACK -> draw SPR.rail[railMask] on top of whatever over[] drew (track over the street = the grade crossing); STATION -> draw SPR.station, and add stations to the no-power SPR.zap-bolt eligibility test when !stationLive; SUB -> draw nothing normally, draw SPR.subwayVent (or a dashed indigo segment) only when UI.mapMode==='transit'. Night branch: an active station uses spr.night lit windows exactly like other service buildings. Draw order over[]-then-rail so track never hides behind a tower.

INSPECT (ui.js openQuery): when city.rail[i]!==NONE add rows — "Transit: Surface rail / Subway / Station"; on a STATION show "Line #k (N stations)", "Status: open / needs 2 stations / no power" (from railNet/stationLive), "~X trips/mo off roads" (Math.round(city.railRiders)); and a "Transit access: railCov[i]" row on ANY tile so the player learns why a nearby zone is/isn't relieved. Budget dialog gains a Transit funding slider row (reuses the M23 slider-table verbatim) and a lastBudget.dept.transit line; advisors.js gains a transit champion entry.

FEEDBACK: setStatus hint on placing a still-unconnected station ("Station built — link it to another by rail to open the line."); one-time pushMsg ticker when a component first reaches >=2 powered stations ("The Metro is open, Mayor! Commuters leave the car at home."), gated by this.metroOpened so it fires once and never on load.

STATION POWER — the one subtlety the plane introduces (verified against recomputePower, sim.js 486-548): powered[] is only ever set on over[] tiles (conductors + plants + consumers). A station on over[i]===NONE is therefore never powered by the existing flood-fill. Resolution that keeps recomputePower ZERO-edit: in recomputeRail, a station is powered iff this.powered[i] || any 4-neighbor this.powered[j] (i.e. adjacent to a powered wire/zone/crossing). Players wire a station the same way they wire any building — run a power line next to it. Stations are NOT added to powerDemand in v1 (a documented minor simplification; a station is a negligible draw and adding it would require touching recomputePower's demand accounting).
design.simIntegration:
NEW recomputeRail() (place right after recomputeAccess, ~627), deterministic, no RNG:
1. railNet.fill(-1); stationLive.fill(0); a small stationsPerComp count array.
2. One O(n) 4-connectivity flood-fill over rail[i]!==RL.NONE cells using an explicit Int32 stack in ASCENDING-INDEX scan order (never Set/Map iteration order), assigning component ids; TRACK/SUB/STATION all conduct, so a STATION cell fuses an adjacent surface segment with an adjacent subway segment — that is how stations "link modes." Count STATION nodes per component.
3. Station pass: const powHere = this.powered[i] || any N4 this.powered[j]; stationLive[i] = rail[i]===RL.STATION && powHere && stationsPerComp[railNet[i]]>=2 ? 1 : 0.
4. railCov.fill(0). Stamp catchment by copying stampCoverage's body verbatim (sim.js 839-856) but gated on stationLive[i] instead of over/anc/powered: R=Math.round(RAIL_STATION_R*(0.4+0.6*f)) with f=this.funding.transit/100, and out[j]=Math.max(out[j],Math.min(255,Math.round((R-d)*18*f))) over manhattan d<=R. f<=0 early-returns (0% transit funding = zero coverage AND, via deptCosts, zero upkeep — a real monotonic lever). A lone / unpowered / disconnected station stamps nothing, so there is no free congestion relief from a dead stub.
5. Metro ticker: if (!this.metroOpened && any stationsPerComp[c]>=2 with a live station) { this.metroOpened=true; if(!silent) this.pushMsg("The Metro is open..."); }. recomputeRail(silent) is called with silent=true from deserialize so a loaded open line never re-celebrates.

THE LOAD-BEARING HOOK — recomputeTraffic() (sim.js 662-688), the single substantive behavioral edit. At the top: this.railRiders=0. Inside the per-zone loop, after `const trips = 4 + this.lvl[i]*9` and before the walk:
    const share = this.railCov[i] ? Math.min(RAIL_MAX_SHARE, this.railCov[i]/255) : 0;
    const roadTrips = trips * (1 - share);
    this.railRiders += trips * share;
then substitute roadTrips for trips at the emission/walk accumulation (load[cur] += roadTrips, line 674). The random-walk (the only RNG here — the reservoir pick at 683) is UNTOUCHED; we scale the injected volume by a float derived from a deterministic map, adding no new nondeterminism. Fewer trips near stations -> lower load[] -> lower traffic[] on those roads = the measurable congestion relief the brief demands. DOWNSTREAM IS AUTOMATIC (zero extra code): trafficNear() drops near stations, so growthPass congestion-damping eases and rail-served zones climb a density level (the classic SC2K "rail enables density" payoff); recomputeMaps diffuses the lower traffic into the land-value penalty; winter's 0.72 road scaling still clears roads seasonally while riders hold steady.

CADENCE / ORDER (tick, sim.js 1304-1308): stations read powered[], so recomputeRail MUST run after recomputePower and before recomputeTraffic. Replace the power block with:
    const doPower = this.powerDirty || this.tickCount % 10 === 0;
    if (doPower) { this.recomputePower(); this.recomputeAccess(); }
    if (doPower || this.railDirty) { this.recomputeRail(); this.railDirty = false; }
    if (this.tickCount % 5 === 0) this.recomputeTraffic();
recomputeRail reads the just-refreshed (or still-valid) powered[]; a pure rail build sets only railDirty (power unchanged) and reads the existing valid powered[]. recomputeTraffic reads railCov read-only every 5 ticks — the ~10-tick refresh latency of railCov matches the existing service-coverage latency and is intentional.

PLACEMENT (canPlace ~373 / place ~409 / bulldoze ~456): add a rail branch BEFORE the generic over[] footprint loop (like the waterfill early-out), dispatched by tool id:
- canPlace: rail(TRACK) requires rail[i]===NONE && over[i] in {NONE, ROAD, WIREROAD} (grade crossings on roads are allowed; zones/buildings refuse), water allowed as a bridge; subway(SUB) requires only rail[i]===NONE (tunnels under any over[] and any terr including water — its superpower); station requires rail[i]===NONE && over[i]===NONE && terr!==WATER.
- toolCost: surface rail over water *5 (bridge, reuse the water branch at 404); subway flat cost anywhere.
- place: write this.rail[i]=RL.TRACK/SUB/STATION, charge cost, set this.railDirty=true (NOT powerDirty — rail doesn't change the grid), devRev++; station returns a status hint. 1x1, no anc bookkeeping on the rail plane.
- bulldoze PEEL RULE: if this.rail[i]!==RL.NONE, clear the rail feature first (one click) and set railDirty, else fall through to the existing over[] removal — so razing a zone leaves the subway beneath it intact (two-step removal). Add this.rail[i]=RL.NONE (+railDirty) to the waterfill branch (425) so flooding never leaves a ghost line.

BUDGET (deptCosts ~1110 / collectBudget ~1135): in the deptCosts scan also tally surface=Σ(rail===TRACK), subway=Σ(rail===SUB), stations=Σ(rail===STATION); add to the returned object transit: Math.round((surface*0.3 + subway*0.5 + stations*20) * f.transit/100). In collectBudget fold dc.transit into serviceCost (or a dedicated line) and net, and into lastBudget.dept.transit. Because stampRail scales catchment by f.transit AND deptCosts scales upkeep by f.transit, cutting Transit funding shrinks ridership AND cost monotonically — a genuine tradeoff, identical in spirit to police/fire.

UNCHANGED BY CONSTRUCTION: recomputePower, recomputeAccess, growthPass, recomputeMaps diffusion, and every over[]===ROAD/WIREROAD predicate — none see a new value because rail lives off over[]. This is the whole payoff of the plane decision versus the Depth lens's fused RAILROAD.
design.saveImpact:
Bump serialize() v:8 -> v:9 (sim.js ~1360).

EXACTLY ONE new serialized field: rail: Array.from(this.rail) in serialize; guarded restore in deserialize: if (Array.isArray(d.rail)) c.rail.set(d.rail); (else the ctor's zeros stand). rail[] is the sole authored transit state — the physical network (surface track, subway, stations) lives entirely in it. railNet, stationLive, railCov, railRiders, railDirty, metroOpened are ALL derived and MUST NOT be serialized; they are rebuilt on load exactly like access/traffic/pollution/coverage today.

ONE new persisted funding key: add transit:100 to the funding literal in BOTH the constructor (~304: {police,fire,roads,edu,health, transit:100}) AND the deserialize Object.assign default map (~1398: Object.assign({police:100,fire:100,roads:100,edu:100,health:100, transit:100}, d.funding||{})). Because funding is serialized wholesale and deserialize already merges over defaults, a v8-or-earlier save with no transit key loads at 100% and plays identically — no migration code.

deserialize recompute chain (~1426): change `c.recomputePower(); c.recomputeAccess(); c.recomputeTraffic();` to insert the rail rebuild between access and traffic: c.recomputePower(); c.recomputeAccess(); c.recomputeRail(true); c.recomputeTraffic(); ... then c.railDirty=false; c.metroOpened = (any live >=2-station component) — set silently so a loaded open Metro never re-fires the ticker (recomputeRail's silent=true already suppresses the pushMsg; the metroOpened flag it sets carries forward).

BACK-COMPAT: a pre-M25 save has no rail field -> rail stays all-zeros -> railCov all-zero -> recomputeTraffic's share is always 0 -> traffic behaves EXACTLY as before (zero behavioral drift on existing cities). No existing field changes meaning; no OV enum value shifts (rail is a separate plane, over[] bytes load verbatim), so this composes cleanly with M26's WIREROAD=18 under a single monotonic v9 — coordinate with M26 so both land as additive v9 fields (rail[] + funding.transit are independent of WIREROAD's over[] value). The v9 bump documents the new rail[] array and funding.transit key. Old-build-loading-new-save (a pre-M25 build opening a v9 save with rail tiles would simply ignore rail[] and mis-omit those lines) is the normal one-way forward caveat the version bump flags.
design.risks:
DETERMINISM (safe by construction): recomputeRail is an ascending-index flood-fill (explicit Int32 stack, no Set/Map order dependence) + a coverage stamp — both deterministic; component ids need only be internally consistent within a tick since only the per-component station COUNT is consumed. The traffic diversion scales trips by a float from a deterministic map and adds NO new RNG; the sole randomness (the pre-existing reservoir walk) is untouched, and diversion happens BEFORE the walk, never inside the reservoir pick. Per-seed reproducibility and save round-trip parity hold. GUARD: a save-roundtrip test that stamps a rail line + 2 powered stations, ticks N, serializes/deserializes, and asserts identical railCov/traffic/railRiders.

REGRESSION SURFACE (minimized, the big win over the Depth lens): keeping rail off over[] means no t>=OV.ZR / isPlant / demand / growth / flammability / complaint / roadWear / roadMask scan ever sees a new value, so none can misbehave — versus the Depth lens's ~12 road predicates that each had to learn RAILROAD or silently break a crossing. The only touched sim functions are recomputeTraffic (one guarded block), deptCosts/collectBudget (additive), canPlace/place/bulldoze (one new branch), tick (one guard line), deserialize (one call) — all additive and independently testable.

STATION-POWER edge (flagged during synthesis): recomputePower only powers over[] tiles, so a plane station is powered by ADJACENCY (powered[i] || any N4 powered[j]) computed in recomputeRail. Consequence: a station not next to a powered tile is inert (correct — surfaced via the no-power SPR.zap bolt + inspect "no power" + status hint, never a silent no-op). It also means stations don't add to powerDemand in v1 (documented simplification; negligible draw). If later we want stations as real consumers, that is a localized recomputePower edit, not a redesign.

BALANCE / FUN: RAIL_MAX_SHARE=0.60 and the >=2-powered-stations gate are the knobs. Too high trivializes congestion and warps demand/growth; too low makes rail a chore. Target feel to playtest: a gridlocked arterial visibly cools on the traffic minimap within a month of a line opening, and a served zone climbs a density level it was stuck below. Worst case the effect degrades gracefully to "roads as before" (it is purely a reduction of injected trips). ENHANCEMENT (note, not v1): weight ridership by whether a line connects DIFFERENT zone types (res<->job) so players are rewarded for wiring real commutes — deepens the decision with no new save state.

PERF: recomputeRail is O(n) flood-fill + O(liveStations * R^2), R=7 (cheaper than police R=12), same class as recomputePower+stampCoverage on the same cadence; gated by railDirty/doPower so it idles when no rail exists (early-out when zero STATION cells). Two arrays (railNet Int32, railCov Uint8) + the ephemeral stationLive of size n. Negligible at MAP<=128; no O(n^2). Stations cost §300 so spam is self-limiting.

DEPARTMENT SURFACE: adding funding.transit touches the hardcoded department lists in the budget dialog loop (ui.js) and advisors.js DEPT_CHAMPION — both must gain a transit entry or the slider/advisor silently drops it. Low-fidelity fallback if the extra lever is unwanted: fold rail upkeep into funding.roads and drop the ridership funding scalar.

EDGE CASES: (1) bulldozing one tile of anything is 1x1 on the rail plane, and razing a zone over a subway leaves the tunnel (peel rule) — must set railDirty and the cursor legality preview should reflect two-step removal or players get confused; note it in F1 help. (2) waterfill over rail clears rail[i] (added to the waterfill branch) or a ghost line survives underwater. (3) over-relief emptying roads and killing traffic complaints — RAIL_MAX_SHARE caps at 0.60 and clamps so arterials lighten but never zero out; trafficNear/COMPLAINT_T still function. (4) render draws over[] then rail so track never hides behind towers; UI/small-screen: three toolbtns flow into the existing 64px flex-wrap grid free, and the 8th .mm button may wrap the mapmodes strip to two rows on the narrowest panel — acceptable, but verify the mm-legend line still fits. M26 COORDINATION: agree on a single v9; rail[]+funding.transit are additive and orthogonal to WIREROAD, so they compose without conflict.

criteria.statement: Zero console errors and clean determinism during the whole exercise: loading the page, entering a city, placing rail/subway/station, toggling the transit minimap, ticking, and save/reload produce no console.error / uncaught exceptions; and because diversion scales a deterministic map before the untouched reservoir walk, two runs from the same seed with identical rail edits yield identical railCov and railRiders.

newProposals.title: Neighboring Cities & Regional Connections
newProposals.brief: Give the map's four edges named neighbor cities you can wire into. Roads, rails (post-M25), and power lines that reach a border tile open a 'connection' the player can negotiate through a Win95 deal dialog: sell surplus power to a neighbor for monthly income, buy power when your own plants brown out, or open a highway/rail link that adds a steady exogenous demand bump to adjacent zones (commuters from next door). Neighbors have deterministic per-seed personalities (a hungry industrial town that always buys power, a rich bedroom suburb that floods your commercial zones with shoppers). Deals are month-billed through the existing budget line and serialized.
newProposals.whyItMatters: Regional interconnection is the single most-requested SC2K feature a 1997 fan remembers — the sense that your city is a node in a living region, not an island. It reuses the power flood-fill (a sold-MW deal is just a virtual sink/source on recomputePower's supply/demand sum) and the budget-line + advisor patterns already in place, so it deepens the economy without a new subsystem from scratch, and it gives late-game surplus power an actual purpose.
criteriaSketch: A road/wire/rail tile touching a map-edge border tile registers an active connection to exactly one of four named neighbors, and the connection's presence round-trips through serialize()/deserialize() at the new save version

Selling N MW to a neighbor reduces available supply in recomputePower() by N and adds a fixed §/MW to the monthly budget net; buying N MW adds it to supply and subtracts from net — both visible in the budget dialog
Each neighbor's name, personality, and initial disposition are a pure deterministic function of the city seed (two cities from the same seed produce identical neighbors)
An open highway/rail link raises effective demand for zones within K tiles of that edge, measurable as higher growthPass() upgrade rate near a connected border vs. an unconnected one

newProposals.title: Arcologies & Wonder Landmarks
newProposals.brief: Add the four SC2K arcologies (Plymouth, Forest, Darco, Launch) plus a small set of placeable wonder landmarks (a Statue-of-Liberty homage, an Eiffel-style tower, a great pyramid) as large multi-tile OV.* buildings unlocked through the existing tier/reward system. Arcologies are self-contained mega-structures: each houses a big fixed population and job count, is self-powered, and emits its own pollution/land-value footprint, letting a maxed-out city keep growing vertically. Landmarks are prestige objects that pump land value and civic pride across a wide radius (like a super-park) and light up at night. Both are procedural canvas sprites in the established isometric style.
newProposals.whyItMatters: Arcologies were the iconic aspirational end-game of SC2K — the reward that made a fan grind toward a million citizens, and the Launch Arco secretly 'winning' the game. This slots directly into the existing OV_SIZE/anc[] multi-tile machinery, the M4/M-tier reward-unlock flow, and stampCoverage-style radius effects for landmark pride, so it's mostly content + one big-building footprint rather than new sim math, while giving the late game the ceiling it currently lacks.
criteriaSketch: Each arcology is a single OV.* type with an OV_SIZE footprint > 2, placed via the anc[] anchor pattern, and its fixed population/jobs are counted into the census exactly once per structure (not per tile)
An arcology contributes zero net power demand in recomputePower() (self-powered) and still round-trips through save/load with its population intact
Placing a wonder landmark raises land value within its radius using a stampCoverage-style diffusion, and removing it fully reverts that contribution on the next recomputeMaps()
At least one arcology type is gated behind a population/tier threshold and is un-buildable (absent from or disabled in the toolbar) until that threshold is reached

newProposals.title: Expanded Disaster Roster (Earthquake, Flood, Riot, Monster)
newProposals.brief: Grow startDisaster()/disasterTick() beyond fire/tornado/ufo with four classic SC2K catastrophes, each reading from a sim system you already maintain: an earthquake ripples out from an epicenter turning buildings to rubble and starting scattered fires; a flood spreads inland from water tiles along the coastline, damaging low-lying structures; a riot spawns where the crime map is hottest and torches nearby buildings until police coverage suppresses it; and a monster (a Godzilla-homage kaiju) stomps a path across the city like a super-tornado. Each has its own procedural sprite/animation and its own news-ticker flavor, and each increments the yearly disaster counter already in records[].
newProposals.whyItMatters: Disasters are half the joy of a SC2K session, and three is thin for an AAA homage. Crucially these aren't random noise — the riot consumes the crime map, the flood consumes coastline/water terrain, tying calamity to how well the player actually governs, which is exactly the SC2K design ethos. It reuses the existing disaster tick loop, ignite(), rubble conversion, and the coverage/crime maps, so each new disaster is an incremental handler, not a new engine.
criteriaSketch: Each new disaster kind is startable via startDisaster(kind), increments recCur.disasters, and (for the moving kinds) advances through disasterTick() to a clean termination that nulls this.disaster
A riot preferentially ignites in the highest-crime region (its epicenter correlates with the crime map maximum, not a uniform-random tile) and is suppressed faster where police coverage is high
A flood only damages tiles reachable from existing TERR.WATER (inland spread from the coast) and never appears in a landlocked interior with no adjacent water

An in-progress disaster of every new kind round-trips through serialize()/deserialize() and resumes ticking after load, and disabling disasters (disastersEnabled=false) prevents all of them from spawning randomly

newProposals.title: City History Charts & Trend Graphs
newProposals.brief: A Win95-styled 'Graphs' window that plots the city's history over time — population, monthly cash flow, tax income, pollution index, crime index, and land value — as selectable line graphs with 1-year / 10-year / 100-year zoom, all drawn on canvas in the period-authentic bevelled-window chrome. It's backed by the almanac records[] you already serialize plus a lightweight monthly ring-buffer of the diffuse-map aggregates, so history survives save/load. Toggling series on and off and reading a value at a hovered year mirrors SC2K's beloved graph window.
newProposals.whyItMatters: SC2K's graph window is where a mayor felt like a data-driven executive — watching the pollution line cross the population line was a genuine gameplay feedback loop. The almanac already stores per-year pop/taxes/net/disasters, so most of the data pipeline exists; this milestone turns latent saved data into the analytical 'query/data view' the prompt calls for, closing the loop between the sim's diffusion maps and the player's decisions with almost no new simulation code.
criteriaSketch: The Graphs window renders at least six selectable series (pop, cash flow, tax, pollution, crime, land value) from serialized history, and each series can be independently toggled visible/hidden
Historical points are sourced from records[] / a serialized monthly buffer so that after save→load the graphs redraw identically (same points, same shape) with no gap at the load boundary
Switching the time-range (e.g. 1yr/10yr/100yr) rescales the axes and the plotted line without mutating the underlying data, and a city with only a few months of history renders without error
Aggregate values shown in the graph (e.g. current pollution index) match the corresponding value computed by recomputeMaps() for the same tick, within rounding

newProposals.title: Garbage & Waste Management
newProposals.brief: Residential, commercial, and industrial zones generate garbage in proportion to population/activity; the city must dispose of it via a placeable Landfill zone (a paint-style overlay that fills tile-by-tile and permanently scars land value + pollution as it saturates) or, at a higher tier, a WasteToEnergy Incinerator (2x2 plant that consumes garbage and emits pollution but also trickles power). A recycling-center ordinance/building cuts the waste stream. When landfill capacity runs out, uncollected garbage piles up as a growing pollution and complaint source, exactly like SC2K's overflowing dumps.
newProposals.whyItMatters: Garbage was one of SC2K's most memorable 'invisible until it bites you' systems — the landfill that quietly ate your suburbs and tanked land value taught players about externalities. It's a natural sibling to the queued water/sewage utility (M24) but mechanically distinct, and it maps cleanly onto systems already here: a per-capita generation number folded into recomputeMaps, a fill-counter on landfill tiles like roadWear, pollution/land-value penalties via the existing diffusion, and an incinerator that reuses the POWER_CAP/isPlant plant machinery.
criteriaSketch: Total garbage generated per tick is a deterministic function of zoned population/jobs, and total landfill+incinerator capacity is compared against it to produce a shortfall that round-trips through save/load
A landfill tile accumulates a serialized fill counter (like roadWear) and, as it saturates, measurably lowers land value and raises pollution in its neighborhood via recomputeMaps()
An unmet garbage shortfall raises pollution and generates a citizen complaint through the existing complaint system, and adding capacity clears the shortfall on the next recompute
The incinerator is an OV.* 2x2 building recognized by isPlant()/the plant sprite path, contributing a small amount to recomputePower() supply while consuming garbage capacity
